source_native_prescreen.evidence: Four participants made rapid choices from noisy luminance difference stimuli sampled per 13.33ms frame with corrective changes allowed. Initial/final response traces are directly observed, model latent accumulator is unobserved.
Source reports changes on 23.91 percent trials (18.53 percent corrected errors; 5.38 spoiled correct) and initial/final correct 66.95/80.10 percent; do not generalize independent N beyond four.

source_native_prescreen.locator: original Fig1 first frame and mixed effects
source_native_prescreen.evidence: Strength of very first sensory frame interacts with initial decision correctness in change of mind probability (source chi-square 42.08 and p below 8.75e-11) and speed association is weaker (source chi-square 4.27 p=.039); behavioral association does not directly identify a unique neural snapshot mechanism.

source_native_prescreen.locator: published extended-diffusion computational Methods and Fig2
source_native_prescreen.evidence: Initial frame snapshot persistent internal starting/initial-drift contribution to postdecision evidence accumulation plus across-trial drift variability; simulated psychophysical kernels predicted using fit to behavioral responses only, not directly fit to entire measured evidence-stream kernel.

Model without initial snapshot first-frame dependence predicts opposing or absent early signature; version without cross-trial drift variability fails key early differential kernel; retain these source-specific unsuccessful alternative predictions.

Empirical psychophysical traces, first-frame statistical tests, modeled latent dynamics and measured motor changes cannot be identified with each other; supplement-only adverse model parameters and individual nulls remain unresolved.

known_limits: N=4, unusually many repeated trials; sample-person generalization limited
rapid first frame fixed presentation plus sensory integration filtering confounds across time
multiple corrective changes and trial exclusions affect measured kernel
extended-DMM drift variability and first-frame persistence fit not unique physiological proof
movement trajectory/response timing are observation boundary, not same latent decision variable
unacquired model-critical original supplements contain adversarial tests and auxiliary competing variants
